blog_summary: The blog post discusses a paper from Google DeepMind that presents a breakthrough in unsupervised learning of 3D structure from 2D images. Adrian Colyer highlights the paper's key contribution: demonstrating for the first time the feasibility of learning to infer 3D representations of the world purely from unsupervised data. The approach uses an end-to-end deep learning model with an inference network that encodes 2D observations into a latent 3D representation and a generative network that reconstructs images from this representation using techniques like OpenGL rendering. The model leverages sequential generative models and can handle different 3D representations (volumetric, mesh, or primitives). Colyer emphasizes the model's robustness and scalability, showcasing its ability to perform tasks like 3D scene completion, class-specific generation, and coherent scene understanding. The experiments demonstrate high-quality 3D reconstructions and plausible variations in generated scenes.
paper_title: Unsupervised Learning of 3D Structure from Images
paper_abstract: A key goal of computer vision is to recover the underlying 3D structure that gives rise to 2D observations of the world. If endowed with 3D understanding, agents can abstract away from the complexity of the rendering process to form stable, disentangled representations of scene elements. In this paper we learn strong deep generative models of 3D structures, and recover these structures from 2D images via probabilistic inference. We demonstrate high-quality samples and report log-likelihoods on several datasets, including ShapeNet [2], and establish the first benchmarks in the literature. We also show how these models and their inference networks can be trained jointly, end-to-end, and directly from 2D images without any use of ground-truth 3D labels. This demonstrates for the first time the feasibility of learning to infer 3D representations of the world in a purely unsupervised manner.

figures.title: Motivation: The 3D representation of a 2D image is ambiguous and multi-modal.
figures.caption: The 3D representation of a 2D image is ambiguous and multi-modal. We achieve such reasoning by learning a generative model of 3D structures, and recover this structure from 2D images via probabilistic inference.
